# Find the Array Concatenation Value.

@example 4 and 3 give 43, then 25 and 7 give 257: 43 + 257 = 300.
[4,25,7,3]
=> 300

@example 12 and 80 give 1280, then 5 is left on its own: 1280 + 5 = 1285.
[12,5,80]
=> 1285

@example A single element is added as it is.
[600]
=> 600

# The smallest input.
[1]
=> 1

# A single element at the bound.
[10000]
=> 10000

# One concatenation of the largest values.
[10000,10000]
=> 1000010000

[9999,9999]
=> 99999999

# The first element's digits come first: 213, not 321.
[21,3]
=> 213

# Powers of ten have one digit more than their exponent:
# 5100 + 999 + 100010 = 106109.
[5,9,1000,10,99,100]
=> 106109

# 9 has one digit, 10 has two: 19 + 110.
[1,1,10,9]
=> 129

# Odd length: the middle element is added once, as itself: 13 + 2.
[1,2,3]
=> 15

[10000,10000,10000]
=> 1000020000

# The total (5 * 1000010000) needs more than 32 bits.
[10000,10000,10000,10000,10000,10000,10000,10000,10000,10000]
=> 5000050000

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[3,3,566,100,390,10,808]
=> 570608

@gen 2 small
[100,1,1000,34,9149]
=> 1010283

@gen 3 small
[6,1398,1,5,8536,58,6,10000]
=> 682680

@gen 4 small
[44,95,762,3]
=> 96205

@gen 5 small
[20,179,6209,10000,29,987]
=> 620948916

@gen 6 small
[458,4299]
=> 4584299
